title: The cyclic section-vocabulary null changes specificity when the same pages are reordered
statement: I crossed three orders of fixed public layouts, three paragraph-stream assignments, and 20 paired synthetic backgrounds at each of 31, 62 and 124 pages. On 62 pages in manuscript order, the cyclic test at alpha 0.05 falsely rejected 0 to 1 of 20 unplanted samples per assignment. Section-blocked order gave 0 of 20 in all three assignments, and page-shuffled order gave 20 of 20 in all three. On 124 pages, the manuscript and blocked orders gave zero false rejections, and page-shuffled order gave 18 to 19 of 20. At a 10% plant, the cyclic test on 124 pages detected 20 of 20 plants per assignment in manuscript order and 0 of 20 in section-blocked order. On the shuffled layout the high unplanted and placebo rejection rates accompany high planted rejection. There is no uniform specificity or power across these layouts. Counting only paragraph lines, the original section assignment has the largest weighted section entropy among the rotations in all three page-shuffled layouts. That rank depends on page size and order prior to generating words. This geometric diagnostic does not isolate all causes of the observed false-positive variation.
check: Test a page-label null that preserves or closely matches the amount of eligible paragraph text per section whenever labels are reassigned. Fix a support rule and candidate tolerance before scoring, verify enough distinct reassignments to reach the declared alpha, and use additional fixed public layout orders and paired unplanted, planted and within-length placebo backgrounds. Compare randomization rank, eligible support, false-positive rate and power with the existing three nulls at each page count.
method: Select eligible pages from ZL public practice training only. Reproduce the published sample from seed 408, reserve 124 pages for layout, and learn a new implementation of the fixed two/four-glyph transition tables on the remaining 68 pages. The original executable was unavailable. The reconstruction has ordinary and opener starts and 25% whole-word reuse for familiar words in a rolling memory of 300, with no mutation or moving training window.

Use manuscript order, sections grouped alphabetically with manuscript order preserved within section, and one seeded permutation of intact pages. At a fixed page count each order has exactly the same pages, section counts and paragraph lines. The counts are nested as in the prior experiment.

Route each layout through two independently generated streams using the observed opener slots, one shared writer using random opener-style lines at the global opener fraction among all line slots, or the two streams with rounded common opener fractions among paragraph slots in each section. The shared writer retains a common rolling state and lowers the expected opener-style exposure among selected paragraph lines. The balanced selections fix each section's opener count to rounding; individual slots can change across orders.

Use all four published doses. Plant four novel length-matched marker types per section and length in nested prefixes of randomly ranked eligible words of at least four characters. In the paired placebo shuffle the exact assigned markers among the same affected positions separately by length. This preserves token counts, positions, and marker multiplicities.

Compute F-018's raw section-word mutual information in bits for certain paragraph words. Compare against 199 shuffles of all tokens before selection, 199 whole-page label permutations, and all cyclic offsets of the page labels. Keep the P positions fixed in each null and recompute the affected marginal counts. Include the identity in p-value denominators and count numerical ties conservatively.

The primary alpha is 0.05 as in the historical calibration. At alpha 0.01 an exhaustive rotation of 31 or 62 pages cannot attain the cutoff. Within each design cell intervals are Wilson intervals over 20 backgrounds. The same seeds are paired across the layout and routing conditions. The additional line-count entropy calculation is a descriptive diagnostic run after the primary plan was fixed.

reproduction.run: In a checkout at the runtime revision with pinned data available, place these scripts and plan.json beside the checkout. From the checkout set PYTHONPATH=.:.., PYTHONHASHSEED=0 and OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1. Run python3 ../calibrate_sections.py 1 > ../pilot.jsonl and python3 ../calibrate_sections.py {2..20} > ../remaining.jsonl. Run python3 ../layout_entropy.py > ../layout_entropy.json from the checkout. Run the summary script from the work folder.

layout_entropy.py.text:
"""Check whether cyclic rotation changes section entropy before any words are generated."""

from collections import Counter
import json
from math import log2

from calibrate_sections import prepare


def entropy(counts):
    total = sum(counts.values())
    return -sum((value / total) * log2(value / total) for value in counts.values() if value)


def describe(layout):
    counts = Counter(page for page, _, line, _ in layout.items if line.unit == "P")
    labels = layout.page_labels
    assignments = []
    for shift in range(len(labels)):
        grouped = Counter()
        for page, count in counts.items():
            grouped[labels[(page - shift) % len(labels)]] += count
        assignments.append(grouped)
    entropies = [entropy(grouped) for grouped in assignments]
    observed = entropies[0]
    return {
        "size": layout.size,
        "order": layout.order,
        "section_paragraph_line_counts": dict(assignments[0]),
        "observed_section_entropy_bits": round(observed, 6),
        "unshifted_entropy_rank": sum(value >= observed - 1e-11 for value in entropies),
        "largest_entropy_bits": round(max(entropies), 6),
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    layouts, _, _ = prepare()
    print(json.dumps([describe(layout) for layout in layouts], indent=2))
